sources.caveat: All three topics share one 53-field schema. TWO DEPTH LIMITS ARE CARRIED, not one - 'Maks dybdegraense' and 'Hoveddistributions dybdegraense' - and the Danish indicator uses only the main-distribution one, so K11's threshold test can be run against either. 'Maks dybde begraenset af' names WHY the transect stopped, which is the field that separates a depth limit set by light from one set by substrate, and it is exactly the distinction K11 needs. WHAT IS ABSENT and matters: no shoot density, no biomass, no tissue chemistry of any kind. So K3 (tissue micronutrients) and T1 (tissue sulphide) have no monitoring source in Denmark at all - the vegetation programme measures how much of the plant is there and how deep, never what is in it. sources.name: The complete ODA marine parameter space - what is provably not in it
sources.url: https://odaforalle.au.dk/ topic.aspx?id=h&t=h - the whole Hav topic tree, enumerated
sources.spatial: n/a
sources.aggregation: n/a
sources.parameters_note: The Hav module has exactly ten root topics: Bundfauna, Vegetation, Vandkemi, Feltmaaling, Sedimentkemi, Observationssted, MFS i biota, Maaledybde, Marint affald, Plastik i biota. sources.caveat: Enumerated rather than assumed, and it settles a row of hypotheses at once. (1) SURFACE-SEDIMENT CHLOROPHYLL is in neither sediment topic - Sedimentkemi/Sporstof offers six parameters (Gloedetab, total N, Fe-adsorbed P, total P, dry matter, density) at 18 stations and Sedimentkemi/MFS offers TOC, loss on ignition and clay+silt fraction at 38, so D8's microphytobenthic biomass term has no Danish monitoring source. (2) No sediment P FRACTIONATION - total P and one Fe-adsorbed fraction is the whole of it, which is S4's point made for us. (3) No tissue elemental analysis of any primary producer, so K3 has nothing. (4) No dissolved trace metals, no iron speciation, no selenium, no B12, no thiamine in the marine water column - K5, K6, K9 have nothing. (5) Nothing surface-active: no TEP, no surfactant, no UV filter, no oil-in-water, no DOC and no TOC in the water column, so J1, J2, J3, J4 and J7 have no Danish monitoring source at all. The marine water-chemistry topic is eleven parameters wide, full stop.

sources.custodian: ICES Data Centre (DOME), republished by OBIS/EurOBIS
sources.url: https://api.obis.org/v3/occurrence?datasetid=46c52e34-73b7-45e6-a2ac-742e4c2058c5&areaid=49 (areaid 49 = Denmark: all); year counts at https://api.obis.org/v3/statistics/years with the same filters

sources.caveat: THIS PARTLY REOPENS THE PREVIOUS PASS'S HARDEST NEGATIVE. That pass concluded Danish marine phytoplankton species counts are collected by Denmark and reachable by nobody, because ODA has no phytoplankton node and VanDa returns 401. Species-level COMPOSITION turns out to be reachable after all, by a route nobody looks down: Denmark reports to ICES DOME, DOME feeds OBIS, and OBIS serves 240,671 Danish phytoplankton occurrences from 1979 to 2023 with dates and coordinates, including identifications like Coscinodiscus granii, Skeletonema marinoi, Pseudo-nitzschia seriata and Mesodinium rubrum. WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS THE NUMBER. The Darwin Core occurrence schema carries presence, not cells per litre; DOME holds the counts as an extendedMeasurementOrFact extension that neither OBIS nor GBIF exposes. So K1's diatom SHARE of the community and K2's composition-against-ratio test both need abundance, and abundance needs a direct DOME extraction with an ICES account. That is a much smaller obstacle than 'the data is closed', and it is the single most valuable follow-up in this pass.

sources.caveat: K3's diagnostic is the standard horticultural one - measure what is in the tissue along a nutrient gradient - and the protocols confirm by their own text that Denmark does not do it. Nothing in NOVANA would detect a copper, zinc, boron or magnesium deficiency induced by macronutrient excess, and nothing in it would detect sulphide in eelgrass tissue either, which is T1's variable. A PANGAEA search for Danish Zostera tissue nitrogen and phosphorus content returned no Denmark-specific dataset, so if this exists at all it is scattered in uncatalogued literature.

L1 asks for the independent evidence that would say whether the modelled reference condition ever existed, and the standard method for producing it - a dated core with diatom or pigment stratigraphy - returns nothing for Danish coastal waters in PANGAEA. Three near-misses sharpen the point rather than soften it: Andren's Baltic diatom cores are at Gotland, not Denmark; the Seidenkrantz group at Aarhus has published exactly this method with Cs-137 and Pb-210 dating and diatoms - for Ameralik Fjord in Greenland (PANGAEA.785207, .785336); and the one recent Odense Fjord core (PANGAEA.983163, 55.4524N 10.4929E, 2023) is a resuspension and N-fixation study with no dating and no diatoms. J1.note: No TEP measurement exists for Danish water, searched twice with disjoint query sets across PANGAEA, HELCOM, Dryad and Zenodo. The nearest is GEOMAR's Boknis Eck series in Kiel Bight, 60-100 km away, which measured TEP monthly in the microlayer and the bulk water for twenty months and stopped in 2013. The method is Alcian blue and it is cheap; the gap is a choice.

J2.note: No Danish sea-surface microlayer sampling of any kind. The PANGAEA hits that mention Denmark are Kiel laboratory mesocosms using natural seawater, not Danish field samples. One partial substitute for the calm-weather prediction: the HELCOM aerial-surveillance spill records carry wind speed and direction at the moment of detection, so film persistence against wind can be tested on oil films even though it cannot be tested on the biogenic film J2 is about.

J3.note: No surfactant is measured anywhere in the Danish system - not in ODA marine water (11 parameters), marine sediment (17), biota (61-91) or the stream module (66, which does carry pesticides, pharmaceuticals and bisphenol A), and not in HELCOM's hazardous-substances programme. J3's prediction that greasiness scales with population equivalent rather than agriculture has no measurement that could test it.

J4.note: One dataset measures all four UV filters J4 names, including three Kattegat stations - but in sediment, in 2015-2017, on the Swedish side. J4 is about the bathing beach in August, and badevand.dk measures only E. coli and enterococci, so there is neither a measurement nor a collection route for the water at the place and season the hypothesis is about.

J5.note: Denmark counts its litter at true measurement resolution - about 64,000 Danish rows across EMODnet's beach and seafloor litter products - and measures no microplastic. EMODnet's microlitter net-trawl layer has zero Danish tows and its floating-microlitter product has no Danish contributor at all. ODA has built tables for marine litter and for plastic in biota, down to the OSPAR fulmar protocol, and exposes zero rows through them. J5's discriminator, microplastic in the microlayer against the bulk, fails at both ends.

J6.note: THE MOST ACTIONABLE FINDING IN GROUP J. Two independent routes. 58,380 Sentinel-1 GRD scenes cover Danish waters continuously from October 2014, free, and the register is right that this makes J6 testable now - the caveat being that detection is work, not a download. And HELCOM's aerial surveillance already provides 918 Danish per-event spill records from 1998 to 2025, each with position, time, area, estimated volume, polluter type AND WIND SPEED AND DIRECTION at detection. Against the AIS traffic this project already holds, J6's discriminator can be run today. What is closed is the operational satellite detection product: CleanSeaNet goes to Miljoestyrelsen and Soevaernet and to nobody else.

J7.note: ODA's marine water chemistry has no DOC and no TOC, so the monitoring cannot see J7's variable at all. One academic dataset can: Roskilde Fjord, 8 stations, 36 dates in 2014-2015, DOC and TOC with the DOM optical proxies (SUVA254, humification index, fluorescence peaks) that separate fresh exudate from refractory material. Three-weekly sampling is coarse against a bloom collapse, and pairing it with bloom PHASE still needs the phytoplankton counts that sit behind VanDa's 401 or an ICES DOME extraction.

J8.note: Refines rather than overturns the earlier F8 blank. Danish marine microbial community composition is absent from MONITORING - ODA has no microbiology node - and present in the RECORD: 436 sequencing runs across six projects for Danish coastal water in ENA, 2019-2023, with dates and coordinates. Most target seagrass-associated or biofilm communities rather than open-water plankton, and none measures exopolymer production, which is the other half of J8's discriminator.

K1.note: BOTH HALVES MOVED. Dissolved silicate sits in the same ODA table as N and P at the same stations and dates, so the Si:N ratio K1 says is almost never reported is one query away. And the species composition the earlier pass declared unreachable is reachable after all: 240,671 Danish phytoplankton occurrences, 1979-2023, through ICES DOME's feed into OBIS. What is still missing is the cell count - OBIS and GBIF strip the abundance extension - so the diatom SHARE needs an authenticated ICES DOME extraction. That is the single highest-value follow-up in this pass.

K2.note: Same position as K1 and the same obstacle. Simultaneous N, P and Si are there; species presence is there; the biomass share that would let composition be regressed on the ratios with absolute concentration held fixed is one extraction away.

K3.note: CONFIRMED ABSENT FROM THE PROTOCOLS THEMSELVES. NOVANA's eelgrass (M18) and macroalgae (M12) technical instructions cover cover percentage, depth limit, shoot density and species composition and contain no tissue chemistry of any kind - no C, N or P content, let alone Cu, Zn, B, Mn or Mg. The vegetation programme maps how much plant is where and never analyses the plant, so nothing in Danish monitoring could detect an antagonism-induced micronutrient deficiency.

K4.note: No Danish thiamine assay. The Swedish M74 series could not be opened - SLU's database listing has no M74 product and the ICES report repository refused automated access - and even when opened, WGBAST publishes frequency per river per year, so the per-female measurement is aggregated away before publication. One Danish thread exists: ENA study PRJEB59221, 'Coastal Vitamin B1 dynamics', Roskilde Fjord 2020.

K5.note: No marine B12 and no dissolved cobalt for Danish or Baltic water; the nearest cobalt work is Finnish sediment porewater. ODA's eleven marine parameters contain neither.

K6.note: No iron speciation for Danish water. GEOTRACES formats were confirmed but its station index could not be opened, so Baltic coverage is unchecked rather than proven absent. The AL561 Kattegat-Skagerrak cruise does carry dissolved porewater Fe at 15 stations, which is sediment rather than water column and total rather than ligand-bound - K6's whole point is that the available fraction is the quantity, and the available fraction is measured nowhere here.

K7.note: ANSWERABLE NOW FROM DATA ALREADY REACHED. K7 needs two of pH, alkalinity, DIC and pCO2; ODA carries pH and total alkalinity in the same marine table at 1,125 historical stations, and salinity and temperature come from the CTD topic at the same places, so aragonite and calcite saturation are a CO2SYS call away. Three honest caveats: pH and alkalinity are far sparser in the extract than the nutrients, the pH scale and alkalinity method are not stated in the parameter name, and Denmark operates no ICOS ocean station - all 38 were enumerated - so there is no domestic pCO2 series to validate the calculation against.

K8.note: The gradient exists only in tissue. Routine Danish marine monitoring measures NO dissolved trace metal in the water column at all - confirmed against ODA's eleven marine parameters and against an OBIS dataset search returning zero. Metals live in mussel tissue at 25 stations, and the 7,017 Danish contaminant-in-biota records reachable through OBIS carry the organism but not the concentration. So K8's full-gradient dose-response has an exposure proxy and no dose.

K9.note: Mercury is measured in Danish fish and mussel tissue; selenium was not confirmed as a determinand anywhere, and the aggregators that expose the Danish biota records strip every concentration value. The Se:Hg ratio K9 needs would follow from an ICES DOME extraction if selenium turns out to be in the determinand list, and that check was not completed.

K10.note: Fully served and needs no new data. Salinity by station, date and depth is in the CTD topic at 1,527 historical stations; species-level fauna with abundance is in the Artsliste topic; K10's discriminator is community composition against salinity VARIANCE rather than mean, which is a computation on both.

K11.note: THE CLEAREST WIN IN THIS PASS. K11 says Kd and depth are both in the record and the product is rarely formed. It is better than that: ODA's Lyssvaekkelse topic publishes LYSPROCENT, the fitted percentage of surface irradiance already evaluated at each measured depth, alongside Kd and the regression diagnostics, at 566 historical stations; the Maaledybde topic pairs Secchi with bottom depth at 1,503; the vegetation topics give the depth limit and, in 'Maks dybde begraenset af', the reason the transect stopped - which is what separates a light-limited depth limit from a substrate-limited one. DCE's own M06 instruction publishes the Secchi-to-Kd conversion, and Secchi runs continuously from 1983 while Kd starts around 2014. Light at the bed against the 11-14% requirement, per area, over four decades, is a join.

K12.note: Neither the removal nor the restoration is published as data. GEUS Marta begins in 1980, after the stenfiskeri era, and holds no extraction volumes; Zenodo returns nothing for Laesoe Trindel; the ministries' own sites surface no stenrev dataset. K12 is testable in principle - a reef rebuild is a dated, located intervention - and the dates and locations have to be obtained from the projects.

K13.note: No Danish seston particle-size spectrum and no filter-feeder larval condition index found; the nearest work is German. Treat as not-found-by-keyword rather than proven absent - DTU Aqua's mussel research is a plausible unindexed holder.

K14.note: ANSWERABLE NOW. K14 says the fauna data carries species-level abundance and it does - 511 taxa, counts and three biomass measures per grab, at 3,468 historical stations, with 409,490 Danish benthic occurrences visible independently through OBIS as a cross-check. The missing half is a trait table, and BIOTIC is live, built for exactly this join, and covers the North Sea species pool. Functional diversity through time is a desk exercise, as the hypothesis says.

L1.note: THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL GAP IN THIS PASS. Fifteen PANGAEA searches across every named Danish water body crossed with diatom, pigment, Pb-210 and Cs-137 return no dated stratigraphy from a Danish coastal core. The near-misses sharpen it: Andren's Baltic diatom cores are at Gotland; the Aarhus group that has published exactly this method pointed it at Ameralik Fjord in Greenland; the one recent Odense Fjord core is undated with no diatoms. The reference condition Denmark spends against therefore has no independent check, and the method to build one exists in the country.

L2.note: The choice is written down and the derivation is not. Decision 2013/480/EU gives the eelgrass depth-limit boundaries for the Danish and German open coast - EQR 0.90 High/Good and 0.74 Good/Moderate, 8.5 m and 7 m - which is the whole difference between passing and failing, agreed rather than measured. The chlorophyll boundary is deferred to an unresolved Annex II, and the four papers that document the Danish reference model are all paywalled with no open data or code. L2's one-line sensitivity calculation is unpublishable by an outsider for that reason.

L3.note: MUCH BETTER THAN THE REGISTER ASSUMED, AND FOR AN UNEXPECTED REASON. L3 says almost every Danish series begins in the 1970s or later, at the loading maximum. The Secchi record in ODA runs unbroken from March 1983 at per-visit resolution, and the historical network is five to forty times larger than the counts in the earlier file suggested. So the start-year sensitivity surface can be computed on a real Danish optical series across four decades. What is still missing is the pre-monitoring evidence, which is L1's gap: without a dated core, there is no way to know whether even 1983 is near a peak or already past one.

L4.note: The decisive evidence L4 asks for exists, once, and is not deposited. The Bisholt transplant in outer Horsens Fjord is a genuine controlled experiment - eelgrass planted July 2017, three treatments with their own coordinates including a bare-bottom disturbance control and a natural donor meadow, fauna sampled four times across 2018-2019 - published open access with summary statistics and no per-replicate data. Denmark's three best-known restoration efforts, NOVAGRASS, ReMAPP and Laesoe Trindel, return zero deposits from Zenodo and NOVAGRASS's own project page now 404s.

L5.note: THE WEAKEST-COVERED HYPOTHESIS IN THIS PASS. The list of Danish areas actually used as reference or least-disturbed sites was not located, so the cross-reference against trawling, dumping and contaminant coverage that L5 asks for could not be started. The ingredients for the second half are all in the earlier file - swept-area ratio, dumping submissions, contaminant coverage - and the first half, the list, is what is missing.

L6.note: L6 is right and worse than it says. The habitat classification for Danish waters is reachable - 23,554 EUNIS/HELCOM HUB polygons over the Kattegat and the Belts - and it is a MODEL, predicted from environmental covariates. Queried for the same box, EMODnet's compiled ground-truthed survey layer returns 18 features and every one is German. So the degraded bed is not merely typed by its present state; for Danish waters it is typed by a model fitted to that present state, with no Danish survey polygons underneath. The history that would make a positive case - charts, stenfiskeri records, oyster beds - was not located and is likely an archive request rather than a download.

R1.note: A C:N CAN NOW BE FORMED FOR PART OF THE PROBLEM. Monthly riverine total N and COD are already at the same stations in ODA Stoftransport, and organic carbon to water is a reported Annex II pollutant for large EU industry - so a discharge C:N exists for the first time. Two things spoil it. TOC in that scheme may be calculated as COD/3 rather than measured, so the ratio can be an arithmetic restatement of what is already known; check the method flag. And FAT IS NOT A REPORTED POLLUTANT ANYWHERE - confirmed by grep across the whole EU specification - so an input with high carbon and zero nitrogen, which is R1's entire subject, is invisible by construction. Whether Danish permits require a measured fat concentration could not be established: the executive order's annexes sit behind a JavaScript app that serves no text.

R2.note: No Danish marine priming experiment. A real one exists 100 km away in the German Bight - 13C-labelled algal protein added to natural sediment and tracked over 400 days - which shows the experiment is standard and that nobody has run it here.

R3.note: THE OBSTACLE IS A JOIN, NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND THE JOIN DOES NOT CLOSE. R3 needs deposited organic matter and its processing state against macrofaunal biomass at the same stations. The fauna is there with three biomass measures. The paired sediment topic at the same stations carries nine grain-size fractions, an oxidised-layer depth and a recorded smell - and NO loss on ignition and NO organic carbon. Organic content lives in Sedimentkemi at 18 and 38 stations, a different and much smaller set, and GEUS's national seabed products carry no TOC layer at all. So the two halves exist and sit at different places.

R4.note: No marine litter-bag or incubation study of characterised recalcitrant fractions along a nutrient gradient, Danish or otherwise. A genuine lignin-phenol depth record exists in the Gotland Basin - one site, Swedish waters, no nutrient gradient - and every nitrogen-by-lignin study that surfaces is terrestrial.

R5.note: The measurements exist and the design does not. Porewater sulphate, methane AND hydrogen sulphide are published at depth resolution for Aarhus Bay from the 2004-2005 METROL cruises, and the AL561 cruise adds a 2021 Kattegat-to-Skagerrak transect. R5's discriminator is explicitly sulphide and methane production against SALINITY ALONG THE DANISH GRADIENT, and what exists is one bay plus one basin transect, neither of which spans the fresh-to-marine transition R5 is about. Note that ODA's marine water chemistry does carry Svovlbrinte as a parameter, so the water-column end is in the monitoring even though the sediment end is not.

R6.note: Every ingredient exists separately and nothing puts them in the same sample. Sequential phosphorus fractionation has been done properly at Bornholm, once, by a Dutch group on an IODP core. In-situ benthic phosphate RELEASE RATES exist at 15 Kattegat-Skagerrak stations. ODA's sediment topic carries an Fe-adsorbed P fraction at 18 stations. What does not exist for any Danish site is a paired sequential iron and sulphur extraction - AVS, pyrite S, ascorbate and dithionite Fe - so the Fe:S ratio R6 is built on cannot be computed.

R7.note: R7 CALLS ITS DATA OBTAINABLE AND IT IS NOT. GEUS's national seabed sediment map classifies the top half metre into about seven texture classes and its only organic content is the qualitative rule that mud means over 10% fine organic matter; MARTA has no organic field; EMODnet Geology's organic-carbon layer is still under development. Danish sediment organic carbon at station resolution is ODA's 18 loss-on-ignition and 38 TOC stations, which are not arranged as a river-mouth transect. AL561 gives TOC along a transect - the wrong one, basin rather than estuarine.

R8.note: Seawater salting-out has been measured properly - for dinitrobenzaldehydes and nitrotoluenes. Never for lipids, anywhere. R8 is the link between group B's imported fat and group J's surface film and it rests on an experiment nobody has run.

R9.note: No comparative decay assay of local against novel material in a marine setting. The standardised Tea Bag Index protocol has been deployed in tidal wetlands in the Americas and never in Denmark.

R10.note: A Crossref search for cross-transplant decomposition across a salinity gradient returns salinity-gradient POWER GENERATION and no biology at all. The salinity gradient itself is fully measured in ODA-CTD; the incubation is not run.

S1.note: DENMARK ACTUALLY RUNS S1's EXPERIMENT, IN SIX CATCHMENTS. LOOP measures leaching from clay and sandy catchments under real management and reports them separately - SR305 gives -0.27 mg N/l/yr on clay against -0.58 on sand across 1990/91-2015/16, plus station-paired soil-water against drain-water nitrate. The medium is mapped at 1:25,000 by genesis class over 93% of the country. Two limits: six catchments is not a national validation of a national map, and the published resolution is annual per station so the event structure is aggregated away. THE FOLLOW-UP THAT MATTERS: the LOOP technical instructions state the raw per-date rows are in ODA, and this project already holds the ODA login the sub-agent lacked.

S2.note: S2 says Denmark holds soil P status and does not carry it into the marine argument. The first half could not be confirmed in open form: no fosfortal, DGT-P, degree-of-saturation or fosforklasse layer by municipality, catchment or ID15 opland exists publicly. The only field-resolution Danish soil P found anywhere is the year-2000 Olsen-P survey of all 731 fields in the six LOOP catchments, 1,365 measurements, published as a sentence in a PDF. The legacy-P argument - the strongest land-side reason a load cut produces no marine response - has no inspectable national evidence base.

S3.note: No sorption-desorption isotherm dataset for Danish soils. The mechanism has been demonstrated on Danish material by Danish groups - Heiberg et al. 2012 on redox-driven phosphate sorption and vivianite - and exists only as papers.

S4.note: S4's point made for us. ODA's marine sediment phosphorus is total P plus one Fe-adsorbed fraction and nothing else. Sequential fractionation of marine sediment P has been done on Danish material once, in Aarhus Bay in 1995, and next door at Bornholm on an IODP core in 2013 by a Dutch group. It is a seventy-year-old method and it is not routine.

S5.note: Bathymetry is held. Sediment thickness is not, in the sense S5 needs. The seabed sediment map carries no thickness at all; the Quaternary thickness raster covers Danish waters but aggregates till and Holocene mud into one column, which is precisely the distinction between reactive and inert that S5 depends on; the NAG-TEC compilation measures basin fill to acoustic basement, kilometres, the wrong quantity. No Holocene mud-thickness product for Danish waters exists.

S6.note: S6's own text says it requires no new measurement at all, and that is right. The national retention map is downloadable in three dated vintages WITH ITS OWN STANDARD-DEVIATION LAYER, so the sensitivity of the indsatsbehov to the retention estimate is computable; the monthly catchment flux series that would be refitted by era is already in ODA. What does not exist is anyone having done it: the vintage differences are model revisions and added virkemidler, not evidence that retention capacity has fallen.

T1.note: THE GAP HAS MOVED AND SHRUNK. T1 needs tissue sulphide, porewater sulphide and light at the bed at the same stations, and says monitoring does not do it. Light at the bed is now clearly available at 566 stations. Water-column hydrogen sulphide is an ODA parameter. Porewater sulphide is published for Aarhus Bay. TISSUE SULPHIDE HAS BEEN MEASURED IN DENMARK EXACTLY ONCE - three sites, one summer, 2012, five turfs each, by Hasler-Sheetal and Holmer - and light was not measured alongside it. So the binding constraint is no longer that light is unmeasured; it is that the plant has been analysed three times.

T2.note: T2 SAYS THE RECORDS ARE IN THE ODA FAUNA DATA IF ANYONE LOOKS, AND THEY ARE. Lucinoma borealis and Thyasira flexuosa are both selectable taxa in the 511-entry Artsliste list, so their abundance and biomass by station and date extract directly; OBIS and GBIF independently confirm 324-373 Danish Lucinoma records and over 7,500 Thyasira flexuosa records back to 1907. The limit is design, not taxonomy: the soft-bottom fauna stations are not placed inside seagrass beds and the occurrence records do not say whether the animal was in one, so 'beds that persist against beds that failed' needs a spatial join between the fauna stations and the vegetation transects, and most will not coincide.

T3.note: Not merely non-routine: ONE SITE, ONCE. Lemvig in Limfjorden, summer 2011, inside a European qPCR survey led from Kiel, reported as site-by-date means with the per-shoot values aggregated away. The fifteen OBIS Labyrinthula records for Denmark are genus-level 18S detections in water or sediment, not diagnoses on a plant, and OBIS returns zero for L. zosterae. The host-stress half of T3's discriminator exists nowhere alongside the pathogen half.

T4.note: Trials exist; T4's design does not. The Horsens Fjord transplant is real, dated, located and controlled, and it measures FAUNA recovery. Nobody in Denmark has run the test T4 actually specifies - transplant into failed ground with and without sediment inoculation from a functioning bed - which is the marine version of the standard horticultural replant-disease assay and would cost very little.

T5.note: T5 says sediment microbial community composition does not exist here; 1,459 Danish sediment BioSamples with coordinates and dates say otherwise. But every confirmed site is open basin or harbour sediment, principally the Aarhus Bay M5 station - none is eelgrass rhizosphere. So the composition exists and the comparison T5 needs, functioning bed against failed bed, has no material at either end, and the transfer assay has not been attempted.

T6.note: No rhizosphere community along a nutrient gradient for Denmark, and no tissue chemistry that would index host stress. T6 is the least-evidenced hypothesis in the T group after T8.

T7.note: Half of T7 turns out to be published and open. Acetate, lactate, formate and propionate are measured at depth resolution in Aarhus Bay cores from December 2004, alongside sulphate reduction rates and methane - so 'porewater organic acids' is not the blank T7 assumes. The other half is genuinely absent: no dissolved Fe(II) or Mn(II) speciation for any Danish site after repeated searching, and no ethylene anywhere. One unexpected proxy: ODA's fauna-sediment topic records 'Oxideret lag (mm)', the measured depth of the oxidised surface layer, at every grab.

T8.note: The entire Danish marine oomycete record is one Limfjorden site inside a Dutch-led multi-country isolation survey. T8's actual claim is that anoxia selects these organisms, and nothing in that paper measures redox, so the causal half is untested rather than unsupported.

D8.note: BOTH VARIABLES ABSENT. Sediment erodibility has never been measured in Danish monitoring - no cohesive strength meter, no flume - and SURFACE-SEDIMENT CHLOROPHYLL is in neither ODA sediment topic, confirmed by enumerating both parameter lists. So D8's microphytobenthic biomass term has no Danish source at all. Two partial substitutes exist and should be named as substitutes: the fauna-sediment topic's nine grain-size fractions and its 'Oxideret lag (mm)', and modelled bed shear stress from the wave reanalyses already held.

D9.note: D9's OWN PREMISE IS WRONG AND THAT MAKES IT TESTABLE. The hypothesis states 'Present design gives one grab per station'. A live extract returned 10 replicate Haps grabs at one station on 2025-05-07 and 7 at another on 2025-03-24, each replicate with ITS OWN latitude and longitude and a stated gear area of 143 cm2. Within-station spatial variance of abundance and biomass - mosaic against homogenised flat, which is the entire discriminator - is computable from data already reachable, across 3,468 historical stations. This is the most actionable single finding in the D group.

D10.note: ANSWERABLE NOW. D10 asks for sediment grain size by station and date and calls it collected historically but rarely analysed as a time series. ODA's fauna-sediment topic carries nine fractions from mud to stones per grab per date at 3,596 historical stations. GEUS's national map is one vintage and cannot give change; ODA can. The time series is a query.

D11.note: Half of D11 is a desk exercise and the other half has no data. The bioturbator-to-biostabiliser biomass ratio can be built today: species-level abundance and three biomass measures from ODA, joined to BIOTIC's forty trait categories. What cannot be done is testing that ratio against MEASURED ERODIBILITY, because erodibility is measured nowhere in Denmark - the same blank that stops D8.

gaps.missing: A dated sediment core with diatom or pigment stratigraphy from anywhere on the Danish coast. Fifteen PANGAEA searches across every named Danish water body crossed with diatom, pigment, Pb-210 and Cs-137 return nothing. The method is standard, the Aarhus group has published it - on Ameralik Fjord in Greenland. The reference condition Denmark is spending against therefore has no independent check, and this is the gap most worth closing.

Any TEP measurement in Danish water. Searched twice with disjoint query sets. The nearest is GEOMAR's Boknis Eck series, monthly, 60-100 km away, which ended in 2013. Alcian blue is cheap and standard.
Any sea-surface microlayer sample from Danish water. The PANGAEA records that mention Denmark are Kiel laboratory mesocosms.

Any surfactant measurement, marine or in receiving waters. Confirmed against all four ODA modules and HELCOM's hazardous-substances programme. Whether a Miljoestyrelsen chemical survey ever measured LAS in Danish effluent is the one thread left unpulled - mst.dk publication paths returned 403 and 404.

UV filters in Danish bathing water, in bathing season. The one dataset that measures all four compounds is sediment, 2015-2017, three Kattegat stations on the Swedish side. badevand.dk measures only E. coli and enterococci, so there is not even a collection route.

Water-column or microlayer microplastic in Danish waters. EMODnet's microlitter net-trawl layer has zero Danish tows; its floating-microlitter product has no Danish contributor; ODA's plastic-in-biota table is built and empty. What exists is 64,000 rows of macro litter.
DOC in Danish marine monitoring. ODA's marine water chemistry is eleven parameters and none of them is organic carbon. The only Danish marine DOC series is one fjord, twenty months, ending 2015.

Phytoplankton CELL COUNTS. The composition is reachable through ICES DOME's feed into OBIS - 240,671 Danish occurrences, 1979-2023 - but OBIS and GBIF strip the abundance extension, so the diatom share needs an authenticated ICES DOME extraction. This is the highest-value follow-up in the pass and it is one account away, not closed.

Tissue elemental analysis of any Danish marine primary producer. Confirmed absent from the NOVANA protocols themselves: M18 and M12 measure cover, depth limit, shoot density and species and analyse nothing.
Any Danish thiamine assay, and access to the Swedish M74 series. Even in the Swedish record the published unit is frequency per river per year, so the per-female measurement is aggregated away.
Marine B12 and dissolved cobalt for Danish or Baltic water.

Iron speciation in Danish water. Total dissolved Fe exists in AL561 porewater; the available fraction, which is K6's whole point, is measured nowhere. GEOTRACES Baltic coverage remains unchecked rather than proven absent.
Dissolved trace metals in the Danish marine water column. Not one, anywhere in routine monitoring. The gradient exists only as tissue burden in mussels.
Selenium in Danish marine biota, and the Se:Hg ratio. Mercury is measured; selenium was not confirmed as a determinand, and the aggregators strip every concentration.

Danish stone extraction volumes and locations for the stenfiskeri era, and reef restoration coordinates, tonnages and dates. GEUS Marta begins in 1980, after the removals, and holds no extraction volumes.
Seston particle size spectra and filter-feeder larval condition indices for Denmark.

The chlorophyll EQR boundary chain and the reference model's assumptions. The eelgrass boundaries are in Decision 2013/480/EU and readable; the chlorophyll boundary is deferred to an Annex II that did not resolve, and all four papers documenting the Danish derivation are paywalled with no data or code deposit.

Per-replicate data from any Danish restoration trial. The Horsens Fjord transplant is published as summary statistics; NOVAGRASS, ReMAPP and Laesoe Trindel return zero deposits from Zenodo and NOVAGRASS's project page now 404s.

The list of Danish areas actually used as reference or least-disturbed sites. Without it the cross-reference against trawling, dumping and contaminant coverage cannot begin. This is the least-covered hypothesis in the pass.

Historical Danish seabed structure - digitised sea charts, stenfiskeri records, oyster bed maps - and, unexpectedly, ground-truth habitat survey polygons. EMODnet's compiled survey layer returns 18 features for the Danish Kattegat and Belts and every one is German, so the Danish habitat classification rests on a model fitted to the present state.

Fat as a discharge parameter. Confirmed absent from the entire EU Annex II pollutant list. Whether Danish permits require a measured fat concentration could not be established because retsinformation.dk serves no text to any fetch; settle it with one named facility's udledningstilladelse. Note also that reported TOC may be calculated as COD/3 rather than measured.
Any Danish marine sediment priming experiment. One exists 100 km away in the German Bight.

Sediment organic content AT the fauna stations. The fauna-sediment topic carries grain size and no loss on ignition; loss on ignition lives in a different, much smaller station set; and GEUS's national seabed products carry no TOC layer at all.
Decay of characterised recalcitrant fractions along a nutrient gradient, marine, anywhere. The one Baltic lignin-phenol record is a single Gotland site with no gradient.

Porewater sulphide and methane ALONG THE DANISH SALINITY GRADIENT. The measurements exist for one bay in 2004-2005 and one basin transect in 2021; the fresh-to-marine transition R5 is about is not spanned by either.

Paired sequential iron and sulphur extraction - AVS, pyrite S, ascorbate and dithionite Fe - on any Danish sediment. Every ingredient exists separately; nothing puts them in one sample, so the Fe:S ratio cannot be computed.
Sediment organic carbon along a salinity transect from a Danish river mouth, and a Danish sediment TOC map of any kind. R7's claim that this is obtainable is wrong.
Lipid partitioning by salinity. Seawater salting-out has been measured for nitroaromatics and never for lipids, anywhere.
Comparative decay of local against novel material in a marine setting. The Tea Bag Index has never been deployed in Denmark.
Cross-transplant incubations across the salinity front. A literature search returns salinity-gradient power generation and no biology.

Danish soil phosphorus status by area. No fosfortal, DGT-P, saturation degree or fosforklasse layer exists in open form at any spatial unit. The only field-resolution soil P found anywhere is a year-2000 Olsen-P survey of 731 fields in six catchments, published as a sentence in a PDF.
Sorption-desorption isotherms for Danish soils. The mechanism is demonstrated in papers and exists as no dataset.
Fractionated sediment phosphorus. ODA gives total P and one Fe-adsorbed fraction. Sequential fractionation has been applied to Danish marine sediment once, in 1995.
Holocene mud thickness for Danish waters. The seabed map has no thickness; the Quaternary raster merges till and mud; NAG-TEC measures to basement.

Eelgrass TISSUE sulphide. Measured in Denmark once - three sites, one summer, 2012, five turfs each. The light-at-the-bed half of T1's triad turns out to be well covered, so the plant is now the binding constraint.
Labyrinthula screening beyond one site. Lemvig, summer 2011, in a Kiel-led European survey, reported as site-by-date means. Nothing measures host stress alongside it.
A transplant trial with sediment treatment - inoculation from a functioning bed against none. The marine replant-disease assay has not been run in Denmark, and it is cheap.
Sediment microbial community from inside a seagrass bed, and any transfer assay. 1,459 Danish sediment BioSamples exist and every confirmed site is open basin or harbour sediment.
Rhizosphere community composition along a nutrient gradient. Nothing at all.
Dissolved Fe(II) and Mn(II) porewater speciation for any Danish site, and ethylene anywhere. Organic acids turn out to be published for Aarhus Bay, so this is the remaining half.
Any pairing of oomycete or labyrinthulid abundance with sediment redox. The whole Danish marine oomycete record is one Limfjorden site in a Dutch-led survey that measures no redox.

Sediment erodibility (cohesive strength meter or flume) AND surface-sediment chlorophyll. Neither is measured anywhere in Denmark; both parameter lists were enumerated to confirm it. This is the only hypothesis in the D group with no Danish data at either end.
Measured erodibility to test the stabiliser/destabiliser ratio against. The ratio itself can be built today from ODA fauna joined to BIOTIC traits.

_caveats.how_this_was_searched: Six parallel research passes - the land side, baseline and counterfactual, sediment sickness, surface film, nutrient depletion, and decay - plus direct authenticated work by the lead inside ODA. The sub-agents had no ODA login; the lead did, and used it. Nothing is listed because it ought to exist.
_caveats.what_the_lead_verified_personally: The complete ODA Hav topic tree, enumerated node by node: ten root topics, their leaves, every criterion option list and every output-field list. Three topics the earlier pass never opened - Maaledybde, Marint affald and Plastik i biota. Live data extracts parsed row by row: 43 rows of bundfauna across two stations, 4,044 rows of Maaledybde, 161,594 rows of Lyssvaekkelse, 1,823 rows of marine water chemistry across two stations, 18,653 rows for one Kattegat station over 2000-2012, and period-filtered samples establishing the Secchi record back to March 1983. The station-count correction was measured directly for nine topics with a fresh session each time.
_caveats.ODA_DATE_FORMAT: OPERATIONAL WARNING THAT AFFECTS THIS PROJECT'S OWN CODE. ODA's period criterion accepts DD-MM-YYYY and silently returns ZERO ROWS for YYYY-MM-DD. scripts/fetch_oda.py set_period() sends 'yyyy-mm-dd', so any run of it with --from and --to produced an empty extract that looks exactly like 'there is no data for this period'. The whole marine record appeared to start in 2025 until the format was changed. Fix set_period() before the next extract, and re-check any conclusion drawn from a dated fetch_oda run.
_caveats.ODA_STATION_COUNTS: SECOND OPERATIONAL WARNING, AND IT CHANGES NUMBERS IN THE EARLIER FILE. The station criterion list is filtered by the period currently set. With no period set it offers only the currently reporting network. Every station count in data_sources.json was read in that default state and is therefore the current network, not the record - CTD 185 against 1,527 historically, marine water chemistry 205 against 1,125, bundfauna 78 against 3,468, sediment MFS 38 against 542, mussel tissue 25 against 327. See source ODA-STATION-COUNTS-CORRECTION.
_caveats.the_shape_of_the_finding: The first pass found Denmark strong on LOAD and weak on DISTURBANCE and TOXICITY. This pass finds a third pattern: Denmark is strong on GEOMETRY and blank on CHEMISTRY OF LIVING THINGS. Light, depth, grain size, cover, species identity, spatial position - all measured at fine resolution and mostly unused. Anything requiring an analysis of tissue or of a molecule that is not a nutrient - eelgrass tissue sulphide, plant micronutrients, TEP, surfactants, DOC, B12, thiamine, iron speciation, selenium, sediment chlorophyll - is absent, and absent by design rather than by accident: the technical instructions say what is measured and tissue chemistry is not in them.
_caveats.the_answerable_now_list: The hypotheses that turn out to be testable from data this project can already reach, with no new source and no new measurement: K11 (light at the bed, from ODA Lysprocent plus bottom depth plus the vegetation depth limits, back to 1983 via the published Secchi conversion); D9 (within-station spatial variance of fauna, from the 7-10 replicate grabs per visit that each carry their own coordinates); D10 (grain size time series, from nine fractions per grab at 3,596 historical stations); K14 and half of D11 (functional diversity, from 511 species-level taxa with three biomass measures joined to BIOTIC traits); K7 (aragonite saturation, from ODA pH plus total alkalinity plus CTD salinity and temperature); K10 (community against salinity variance); S6 (retention refitted by era, from flux data already held); L3 (start-year sensitivity on a 42-year Secchi series); and T2's presence half (Lucinoma borealis and Thyasira flexuosa are both in the ODA taxon list). J6 is one processing step away rather than one query.
_caveats.the_one_extraction_that_would_unlock_mos: An authenticated ICES DOME extraction. Danish phytoplankton composition turns out to be reachable through DOME's feed into OBIS - 240,671 occurrences, 1979-2023 - but the aggregators strip the cell counts. Those counts would move K1, K2, A9 and F7 from partial to testable in one step, and the same extraction would supply the contaminant concentrations that K8 and K9 need. It requires an ICES account, not a negotiation.
_caveats.what_this_pass_could_not_reach: The Danish universities' publication repositories (pure.au.dk, orbit.dtu.dk, findresearcher.sdu.dk search interfaces) and Inter-Research all return 401/403 Cloudflare challenges to automated fetches; the workaround that worked is to resolve a DOI through Unpaywall to a direct file path and fetch that. retsinformation.dk serves no body text to any fetch, which is why R1's fat question is unresolved. All VLIZ-hosted infrastructure (marinespecies.org, emodnet-biology.eu) refused connections throughout, so WoRMS traits and Polytraits are unverified rather than absent. mst.dk exposes an /api/search endpoint returning Lorem-ipsum placeholder content - do not cite it.
_caveats.corrections_to_the_earlier_file: Four. (1) Station counts throughout are default-state, not historical - see ODA-STATION-COUNTS-CORRECTION. (2) 'Danish marine phytoplankton species counts are reachable by nobody outside the system' is too strong: composition is reachable through ICES DOME into OBIS, only the abundance is not. (3) The F8 microbial blank holds for monitoring but not for the record - 436 Danish coastal sequencing runs exist in ENA. (4) A9's 'no N-fixation rate measurement exists for Danish waters' is contradicted by the 2023 Odense Fjord dataset, which reports N2 fixation rates directly.
